Put agents onto saved workflows. You are continuing a branch that already carries the agent registry, the spawn plumbing, and the run form / template / run API surfaces. Read `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` and `git diff <base>...HEAD` first, plus the CLAUDE.md section the foundation run added — its capability and ambient-agent decisions are binding on you.

# Read first

`CLAUDE.md`'s workflow invariants in full. The ones that decide this run: a workflow is form input and is NOT a fourth route to `--permission-mode`; a node holds the WORK and names a template for every guard; `promptOverride` is the one exception because prompt text is the half a model may write; an orchestrator block's runs start with nobody looking, which is defensible only because a person fixed its folder, its guard set and its fan-out cap when they saved the graph.

# Build

1. **A `run` block may name an agent**, held on the node beside its mount, folder, task and prompt override — i.e. on the WORK side, not the guard side. Mount and folder are on the node rather than inherited from its template for a stated reason (a template edited months later would silently move a block's run); decide whether an agent follows that same reasoning or follows the template, and write the answer down. `normalizeWorkflowInput` validates it against the agents that exist, taking them as an argument the way it already takes templates, mounts and default isolation — that is what keeps it pure. A block naming a deleted agent is refused BY NAME at save and again at instantiation, never by falling back to none.
2. **`POST /api/workflows/validate`** answers about it through the same `normalizeWorkflowInput` and the same `currentKnowledge()`, and still answers 200 for a refusal. Do not write a second copy of these rules in the client.
3. **The canvas inspector** (`src/components/WorkflowEditor.tsx`, `src/components/WorkflowCanvas.tsx`, `src/lib/canvasGraph.ts`) offers the picker and `BlockStatement` states the agent in its one sentence — that sentence is what the operator approves a press of Run against, so it must say the agent rather than imply it. Nothing about a position or a layout changes; the graph blob must not gain a field `normalizeWorkflowInput` would drop.
4. **An orchestrator block** may name an agent for its own deciding turn, and its `emit_runs` tool may name one per emitted spec — but ONLY an agent that exists, checked in `planEmission` beside the fan-out cap and the cycle check, before anything is created. An agent is prompt-shaped, so this is the same class of thing as the task text `emit_runs` already carries; it must not become a way for the emitted run to reach a guard.
5. **A merge block takes no agent** — it spawns no child at all. Make sure nothing in the editor offers it one.
6. **`workflow_instances`** copies the agent with the graph blob at `startWorkflow`, so editing the workflow cannot move it under an instance already running — the treatment the graph and the instance budget already get.

# Tests

Extend `src/lib/workflows.test.ts` and `src/lib/canvasGraph.test.ts` rather than adding files. Cover: `normalizeWorkflowInput` refusing a deleted agent by name, a merge block refusing one, and `planEmission` refusing an emitted spec that names an agent that does not exist. Only `src/lib` is compiled by `tsconfig.test.json`.

# Verify

    NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev
    npm run typecheck
    npm test
    npm run build

`NODE_ENV=development` is load-bearing — a bare `npm ci` exits 0 while skipping devDependencies and typecheck then fails with exit 127 for an unrelated reason. There is no linter; Docker is unavailable here.

# Rules

Commit on this branch. Do not merge, rebase onto or land anything on the target branch; do not push or open a pull request. Do not touch the chat, dashboard or README surfaces — runs 4, 5 and 6 continue this branch after you. Do not fix unrelated defects; note them in your report.

# Done looks like

A saved graph can put a block on a named agent, the canvas states it in the sentence the operator approves against, an orchestrator block can choose one for itself and for what it emits, a deleted agent is refused by name at save, at validate and at instantiation, a merge block is never offered one, and an instance carries its own copy. Typecheck, tests and build pass. Your report names each acceptance point, how you checked it, and where you decided the agent belongs relative to the template and why.
